sources.title: A bunch of Grand Theft Auto games will be cheap on Steam until GTA 6 comes out, and only one sucks
sources.text: In the run-up to GTA 6 's November 19 launch, Rockstar has multiple classic Grand Theft Auto games on sale on Steam – and, nearest I can tell, only on Steam. The Nintendo Switch eShop actually has a competing deal for the Grand Theft Auto Definitive Edition Trilogy, which is down 67% to $19.79, but that sale ends in 11 hours from the time of writing. On Steam, several GTA games are discounted until November 19 for an obviously timed special promotion. On Steam, you'll find four games on sale via two actual products: You can't argue with GTA 4 for $6, but you might argue with this version of, in particular, GTA 3. The Definitive Edition Trilogy was famously panned at launch for wonky graphics and poor technical performance that, for the most part, has been patched up in the years since. However, the PC port for GTA 3's Definitive Edition is uniquely poorly rated for reasons that will sound familiar. Here's how the three games in this trilogy compare in Steam reviews: The reception to the two other games in the trilogy improved over time while GTA 3 steadily declined. Much like the day-one reviews, today's Steam players complain of Rockstar launcher interference, bugs, shoddy art, broken cinematics, and performance dips. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Curiously, perhaps unrelated to the quality of the port, some of today's gamers also don't seem to take too kindly to GTA 3's design sensibilities, it being slightly older than Vice City and San Andreas, and certainly a rawer open-world experience. Thomas Williamson, the CEO of the outsourced trilogy's original developer, Grove Street Games, said earlier this year that the criticism faced at launch was deserved. "I agreed with most of the people's reactions," he said. "But unfortunately, I feel like we did not agree with how the game was released and the response to it from a development side. And I think that would have changed the narrative significantly." However, he added, "at the end of the day, looking at the behind-the-scenes metrics on those games, there were a lot of people who were playing them and really enjoying them." You won't find Grove Street Games listed on the store pages for these games anymore. Previously, Williamson called it a "dick move" for Rockstar to have Grove Street's name removed. GTA 6 being pirated is just "a fact of life," says CEO of Rockstar owner, and lawyers are ready if it becomes a problem Austin has been a game journalist for 12 years, having freelanced for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, IGN, Sports Illustrated, and more while finishing his journalism degree. He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible. sources.title: Rockstar's having a sale on old GTA games on the only platform Grand Theft Auto 6 isn't coming to (ours)
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 finally arrives on November 19, but not for us, no—the big day is only for gamers on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. We're not being completely excluded, though: We can't have GTA 6 in November, but we can take advantage of pre-release discounts on a bunch of older GTA games—deals that, ironically, don't appear to be available on consoles. As noted by GamesRadar , there are four GTA games available in two releases: Grand Theft Auto 3, Vice City, and San Andreas bundled up in the GTA Trilogy for $19.79/£19.79/€19.79—67% off the regular price—and Grand Theft Auto 4: Complete Edition , which includes The Lost and Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony expansions, for $6/£5.09/€6, a 70% discount. Those aren't the deepest discounts ever seen, but Grand Theft Auto games typically don't venture into the 90% off territory we all enjoy so much—and according to Isthereanydeal.com, this is as low as the GTA Trilogy has ever gone, and close to the mark for GTA 4 . You may recall that the GTA Trilogy Definitive Edition was a mess when it launched in 2021, but it seems to have turned that frown upside-down since then: On Steam, where the trilogy arrived in 2023, Vice City and San Andreas both hold "very positive" ratings. GTA 3 is stuck at a "mixed" rating, which is unfortunate: Glancing at user reviews, it sounds like the game still isn't in perfect shape, but it's also suffering from the fact that it's 25 years old, and was the first 3D game in the series—some jank and roughness was there right from the start. Grand Theft Auto 4: The Complete Edition, on the other hand, doesn't suffer from those shortcomings. It's getting pretty long in the tooth too—it came out in 2008—but represents a shift in design and tone that led the series into what it is today. If you're looking for just one older GTA game to horse around with, this is the one, especially given that it's less than half the cost of the trilogy. As mentioned, these sale prices are currently only being offered on Steam: There's currently no sign of any of them on either the Xbox or PlayStation stores (Fun fact: there actually is no digital version of GTA 4 on the PS Store because Sony didn't start selling full-priced games online until well after 2008). Maybe it's just coincidence, but they do appear to be intentional pre-GTA 6 sales: The discounts are on until November 19, when Grand Theft Auto 6 launches—except on PC. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Will Have 55 Trophies/Achievements
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 is set to be a completionist’s dream. It has been racking up more side content promises than any game to come in the series thus far; there are indications it’s the longest single-player campaign in franchise history, and the world is absolutely gargantuan. That means we can expect a substantial array of GTA 6 Trophies and Achievements to surface, depending on your platform of choice. In fact, thanks to a recent comment on social media, we know how many are coming, and it’s more than Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 5 had at launch. Rockstar Games is all about the ultimate immersion in Grand Theft Auto 6. As they said in a recent interview, they want you to live a life inside GTA 6, which is set to drop in just 11 days, on November 19th. It’s likely the densest Grand Theft Auto title ever made . While you’re immersed, you’ll be able to chase a thick assortment of Trophies and Achievements. The former if you’re on PlayStation, and the latter if you’re an XBOX player, of course. What’s interesting is that Grand Theft Auto 6, with 55 Trophies/Achievements , beats both Grand Theft Auto 5 (51) and Red Dead Redemption 2 (52). It’s not a huge edge, but it’s an edge nonetheless. It’s also worth pointing out that GTA 5 eventually went on to get 78 Trophies/Achievements with the addition of GTA Online content over the years, so there’s every opportunity for GTA 6 to do the same thing. Hell, perhaps this will be the first Grand Theft Auto 6 title to get a single-player expansion since GTA 4. If you want to go the whole hog and 100% Grand Theft Auto 6, you’ll be pleased to know that data suggests there are both a Platinum Trophy and a Mythic Achievement. The latter is the new tier that XBOX put in place in recognition of players who have gone the distance with their games. Grand Theft Auto 6 launches November 19th on XBOX Series X|S and PlayStation 5, and pre-loading will start globally on November 10th. Are you looking forward to GTA 6? sources.title: Zelda Ocarina of Time: All Empty Bottle locations
sources.text: Every Empty Bottle you can earn in Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the N64 and Nintendo Switch Online Empty Bottles are some of the most useful items you can collect in any Zelda game, but especially in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. There are a total of four Empty Bottles for you to collect, and while three of them are relatively easy to access, one is annoyingly tough. Getting a full set of four might be more effort than itâs worth, but grabbing the easy three is basically essential. Weâre breaking down everything you need to know to get every Empty Bottle in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , so just read through the guide below. We have a separate guide if you’re looking for Empty Bottle locations in the Nintendo Switch 2 remake . There are four total Empty Bottles to collect in Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the N64, and the first three can all be earned during the Child portion of the game. Make sure not to forget them! Kakariko Village features the iconic Cucco Lady, and she will ask a young Link to find her seven Cuccos and return them to the pen she stands next to. Return them all, and sheâll reward you with an Empty Bottle. Weâll have a short list of all the Kakariko Cucco locations below. Just remember that entering any buildings or leaving the area will reset the positions of all Cuccos, so you need to do it all in one. Youâll meet Talon and Malon at Hyrule Castle, and once Talon gets woken up, heâll return to the Lon Lon Ranch. Visit Talon inside the ranch to play his Super Cucco Game. You just need to find his three Super Cuccos within the time limit. If you spin your camera toward the crowd of Cucco as the game starts, youâll probably be able to see where the Super Cuccos land, making them easy to find. Once you win, youâll get a bottle of Lon Lon Milk, and you can keep the Empty Bottle after. Unlike the first two weâve covered, this bottle is necessary to progress the story. First you should complete the Dodongoâs Cavern dungeon and progress to Zoraâs Domain. Once in Zoraâs Domain, at the top of the waterfall (connected to King Zoraâs chamber), youâll find the Diving Game. Complete the Diving Game to earn the Silver Scale, which allows you to dive in deeper water. Now you can dive to the bottom of the water in Zoraâs Domain and through the small square cave. This will lead to Lake Hylia. When you surface, look down to see a trail of rupees leading from where you emerged. Follow them, and youâll find a bottle containing Rutoâs Letter. Rutoâs Letter is for King Zora, and heâll let you keep the Empty Bottle after. A good thing too, because youâll need an Empty Bottle for the next area. This is the only Empty Bottle that you must be Adult Link in order to acquire. Itâs also the most annoying by far. The legendary âpot roomâ near the entrance to Hyrule Castle Market Town can be used to farm rupees as a kid, but as an adult, itâs a Poe trading shop. You can trap the spirits of defeated Poes in an Empty Bottle, and then sell them to the Poe Collector. There are ten Big Poes that you can find around Hyrule Field. The Poe Collector will give you 50 rupees for each Big Poe Spirit you give him, and once you give him all ten, heâll reward you with an Empty Bottle. Ironically, it would be a lot easier to farm the Big Poes if we had four Empty Bottles to start with. Each Big Poe can be found around Hyrule Field and will appear if you ride past set spawn areas. Remember that youâll have a maximum of three Empty Bottles at this point, meaning youâll need to take at least four trips to the Poe Collector while farming Big Poes. Each Big Poe cannot be targeted, and you must shoot them with two arrows to take them down. Donât forget to grab the spirit after!

sources.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake devs wanted to nod to the series' notoriously convoluted timeline
sources.text: Developers behind The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's remake supposedly wanted to nod at the series' infamously twisty, hotly debated and convoluted timeline, but series producer Eiji Aonuma thought it would be better to instead focus purely on making the Switch 2 version the best it could be. Eiji Aonuma said as much in an interview with Game Informer , when asked if The Legend of Zelda canon was ever considered during development. "It's funny because the staff would sometimes ask me about the possibility of including nods to the timeline or references to the other game," he recalls, "and I actually, at the time, would say, 'No, let's focus on this game. Let's make this the best version of Ocarina of Time that we can.'" The Zelda timeline notably diverges into three parallel branches after the events of Ocarina of Time - there's the Fallen Hero timeline (Link to the Past, Link's Awakening), the Child timeline (Majora's Mask and Twilight Princess), and the Adult timeline (Wind Waker, Phantom Hourglass). But Nintendo has never placed too much importance on directly connecting these games one way or another, as series creator Shigeru Miyamoto never thought it was "that important." Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom's chronological placements have even been left a little ambiguous (they come after every other Zelda story falls into myth, sure, but are potentially set in an entirely separate Hyrule .) Needless to say, debates around the official timeline will likely persist as long as the series is still kicking. "So, the timeline was in the back of our mind, but we didn't consider taking an approach to this game where we actually, explicitly included references like that," Aonuma adds. Things might get even more complicated with more Zelda on the way next year , though Breath of the Wild director Hidemaro Fujibayashi thinks it's important that new Zelda games don't simply re-use older ideas . Nintendo exec says "new games and remakes both have a place" following Zelda: Ocarina of Time launch Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week Kaan freelances for various websites including Rock Paper Shotgun, Eurogamer, and this one, Gamesradar. He particularly enjoys writing about spooky indies, throwback RPGs, and anything that's vaguely silly. Also has an English Literature and Film Studies degree that he'll soon forget. sources.title: The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina of Time For Switch 2 Could Bring Back A Classic Mode
sources.text: Master Quest might come to the Nintendo Switch 2 remake as DLC Now that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's Nintendo Switch 2 remake has been out for a couple of days, people are already looking for secrets tucked away within the game through datamining. One of the biggest discoveries from that is that Master Quest, which was missing from the remake at release, could be in the works. As Nintendo Everything reported, Bluesky user MrCheeze first discovered references to Master Quest within the game's files on Nov. 6. Then, on Nov. 7, X user OatmealDome added fuel to the fire by claiming that the Master Quest game files needed to be unlocked with DLC, not a simple update. That suggests that Nintendo is planning DLC for this new version of Ocarina of Time , although nothing like that has been announced yet. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Master Quest was first released as a bonus disc included with some copies of The Wind Waker on GameCube, and it makes the classic Nintendo 64 game substantially harder. Master Quest was unlockable after beating Ocarina of Time's 3DS remake once, but it was entirely missing from the Switch 2 remake at release. These datamines confirm that references to Master Quest exist within the remake's code, though, so it seems quite likely that Nintendo would like to bring it to this new remake at some point. Nintendo has not teased Master Quest publicly yet, though series producer Eiji Aonuma's response to IGN when asked about Master Quest certainly hinted at the possibility that it would be worked on post-launch. "So certainly anytime that we release a game, if there’s an opportunity for the devs to consider what might come in the future, we want to leave that possibility open to them and support their interests," Aonuma teased. The remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is available now on Nintendo Switch 2.

sources.name: Polygon
sources.title: Speedrunners Already Breaking The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's Remake
sources.text: The addition of jumping to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has enabled a new speedrunning trick Speedrunners have had their hands on the Nintendo Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for a couple of days now, and some funky tricks have already been discovered. In particular, the remake's addition of a jumping mechanic has enabled new speedrunning tactics that just weren't possible in the Nintendo 64 original or its 3DS remake. Videos from YouTubers like Kethaldo and Knightpohtayto , as well as Bluesky user Mircacle , show how actor jumping is essentially a glitched super jump that players can do with certain aimable tools in Ocarina of Time . To perform the trick, players have to find a movable object, or "actor," in the game's environments, like a chest or movable tombstone. When standing on it, players then have to shoot, press the lock-on button (ZL by default) before it's done being used, and then jump as soon as the animation ends. By doing this, Link can jump much higher than he is supposed to. When used at certain parts of Ocarina of Time's levels, it's possible to jump even higher and skip massive swaths of the game. Right now, it's easiest to pull off when using the hookshot, so actor jumps are worth attempting once you get it. Nintendo has yet to patch this trick out of the remake, so the speedrunning community is avidly taking advantage of it less than a week after the game's launch. Compared to some other speedrunning tricks in the remake , action jumps are very easy to perform, too. When Nintendo decided to add jumping to Ocarina of Time , I'm not sure this is quite what it had in mind. Regardless, it will be very entertaining to see what new speedrunning tricks emerge and how Nintendo responds to or attempts to fix them, as speedrunners spend even more time playing and breaking the remake.

Se veio em busca de novos jogos para jogar através do Xbox Game Pass , está no lugar certo. O serviço ganhou um reforço de peso esta semana com a chegada de seis títulos para os assinantes aproveitarem. Confira abaixo mais informações sobre as novas aventuras! Em Pit of Goblin os jogadores assumem o papel de goblins que precisam explorar masmorras, escapar de armadilhas e fugir de monstros para alimentar o Rei-Rainha Goblin. O jogo aposta no terror cooperativo online, permitindo formar equipes com amigos ou encarar os desafios sozinho. Mas cuidado: se a missão falhar, você pode acabar virando a próxima refeição! Dos mesmos criadores de Vampire Survivors , Vampire Crawlers: The Turbo Wildcard from Vampire Survivors transforma a fórmula de ação do original em uma aventura de exploração de masmorras em primeira pessoa. Com elementos de roguelite e combate por turnos, o game permite montar baralhos de cartas e criar combinações poderosas para enfrentar inimigos e explorar cenários conhecidos da franquia. Void/Breaker é um FPS roguelite em que os jogadores precisam escapar de um ciclo interminável controlado por uma inteligência artificial hostil. Disponível na versão 1.0 para Xbox Series X|S e Cloud Gaming, o jogo traz combates contra máquinas, além de um sistema de modificações que permite criar diferentes combinações de armas e habilidades. Disponível no lançamento pelo Xbox Game Pass, Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School aposta em uma nova abordagem para os jogos de escape room ao apresentar um mundo aberto repleto de enigmas. A aventura pode ser aproveitada em modo cooperativo local ou online para dois jogadores, que precisam trabalhar juntos para solucionar desafios e escapar das salas. Em Firefighting Simulator: Ignite , os jogadores assumem o papel de bombeiros nos Estados Unidos e precisam enfrentar incêndios, lidar com situações de risco e salvar vidas. O simulador permite formar equipes com até três amigos no modo cooperativo ou contar com personagens controlados pela inteligência artificial para auxiliar nas operações. Por fim, MySims Cozy Bundle reúne versões retrabalhadas de dois jogos da franquia: MySims e MySims Kingdom . Os jogadores podem personalizar uma cidade, explorar um reino de fantasia, fazer amizades e participar de diferentes atividades, incluindo a resolução de quebra-cabeças e a construção e decoração de ambientes. O pacote está disponível nos consoles e no Cloud Gaming. Curtiu as indicações para jogar no Xbox Game Pass? Vale a pena dar uma conferida em Void/Breaker , hein? sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: After furloughing its developers and then hiring some of them back, Star Wars Zero Company developer has laid off an unspecified number of staff
sources.text: "While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together." Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid of an unspecified number of developers, after furloughing its entire team and then hiring some of that staff back. As reported by the Star Wars website Bespin Bulletin, several designers of the acclaimed tactics game have taken to LinkedIn to announce that they have been let go by the studio. Among those affected are senior environment artist Ryan Lopez, who worked on the game for three and a half years and has been on furlough for the past three and a half months. "While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together," Lopez wrote in a LinkedIn post . Other designers who lost their jobs include UI Engineer Tyler Eichten and senior quality assurance analyst Ryan Mosher , who spent two years at Firaxis and a further two years at 1047 Games before joining Bit Reactor in October 2024. It's been a tumultuous few months for Bit Reactor. In September, it was reported that the studio had furloughed up to 80% of its staff in the weeks leading up to Zero Company's launch, with the studio having reportedly "run out of most of its money" ahead of the game's launch. At the time, former senior technical artist Zachariah Scott said the project was built with "shocking austerity". Scott also accused Bit Reactor of "concealing the fact that the team was furloughed weeks ago" after the company made the announcement. Within a month, Zero Company had sold one million copies and Bit Reactor subsequently announced it had hired back some of its staff. In a statement posted on Bluesky, CEO Greg Foertsch stated that the furlough had been a response to "unexpected business developments outside of our control" and "necessary to help us eventually bring as many people back as we can". Clearly, though, Zero Company's commercial performance hasn't been enough to bring back everybody. Which is a shame, considering that Zero Company is by all accounts a brilliant Star Wars adventure. Resident word Jedi Ted Litchfield called it "one of the best games of 2026 and a new all-timer Star Wars videogame" in his Star Wars Zero Company Review . Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. Zero Company isn't the only knockout Star Wars game to release this year either, with Star Wars: Galactic Racer providing a similarly scintillating experience in a galaxy far, far away. Indeed, the performance of both games appears to have pleased Star Wars overlords Lucasfilm, and the company is keen to do more creative spins on the universe in the vein of Zero Company and Galactic Racer. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex. Between 2013 and 2022, Rick was games editor of Custom PC magazine and associated website bit-tech.net . But he's always kept one foot in freelance games journalism, writing for publications like Edge, Eurogamer, the Guardian and, naturally, PC Gamer. While he'll play anything that can be controlled with a keyboard and mouse, he has a particular passion for first-person shooters and immersive sims. sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Star Wars Zero Company studio Bit Reactor lays off staff, a month after bringing furloughed developers back
sources.text: "While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together." Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid off an unspecified number of staff, a month after bringing some of its furloughed team back to work. Several developers announced on LinkedIn on Friday, 6th November, that they had been let go, as first reported by Bespin Bulletin . Bit Reactor hasn't said how many people are affected. Among them is senior environment artist Ryan Lopez, who spent three and a half years working on Zero Company, from pre-production to launch, and was laid off after a three-month furlough. UI engineer Tyler Eichten, who worked on much of the on-screen UI for the game's tactical missions, and Ryan Mosher from the QA team have also confirmed they were let go. "While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together," Lopez wrote . "It was a privilege to ship a game with you." Bit Reactor furloughed most of its staff in the weeks before Zero Company launched on 27th August, with one source putting the figure at roughly 80 percent. The studio appeared to have run out of money just short of release. The game did well regardless, and is thought to have sold more than a million copies within a month . Then, in a message shared on Bluesky on 7th October, CEO Greg Foertsch said the studio had "started the process of returning more of our team back to work". Asking staff to step away so close to launch was "an incredibly difficult decision", he said, "but one that was necessary to help us eventually bring as many people back as possible". It's thought more than half the studio returned, though not everyone went back on full pay. It's not clear whether any of those who returned were among the people laid off this week. In Eurogamer's Star Wars Zero Company review , we awarded the game four out of five stars, saying, "an already winning genre is matched with the perfect setting in this earnest, heartfelt, smart and slightly ramshackle turn-based tactics gem".

stories.summary: Ubisoft is reportedly working on two new Assassin's Creed games , and one of them is set in ancient Rome. Read more

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Assassin's Creed is reportedly going to ancient Rome, while a mobile spin-off heads to Jerusalem
sources.text: Ubisoft is reportedly working on two new Assassin's Creed games , and one of them is set in ancient Rome. That's according to YouTuber Xj0nathan, who says the Rome game is codenamed Mars. He claims two sources with access to Ubisoft's backend systems backed up the information, and that the setting will likely be linked to the upcoming Assassin's Creed TV series. The second game, codenamed Pocket, is said to be a mobile title set in Jerusalem. Xj0nathan claims it'll play a bit like Assassin’s Creed Valhalla’s Mastery Challenge, and look similar to the most recent Prince of Persia. The hero's mentor is apparently a character called Myriam. Insider Gaming says it's heard the codenames too, but couldn't confirm them well enough to report them independently. It puts some of that down to the turbulence the franchise has gone through since former Assassin's Creed boss Marc-Alexis Côté left Ubisoft. Last month, the outlet's sources also claimed Assassin's Creed Hexe, the next mainline game, had been delayed internally by another year, likely to 2028. Other reports claim we'll see it next year. If Mars does move into full production, don't hold your breath - Insider Gaming doesn't expect us to hear anything about it until 2029 or 2030. Assassin's Creed has visited Rome before, in 2010’s Brotherhood, but that was the Renaissance version of the city. The leak comes less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series , insisting there are currently no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

sources.name: Polygon
sources.title: Assassin's Creed Hexe Reportedly Delayed As New Assassin's Creed Games Leak
sources.text: Some new insider reporting has shed new light on the future of Assassin's Creed Some new reports regarding the Assassin's Creed series emerged last week, giving us a better idea of what to expect from Ubisoft's flagship series for the rest of the decade. While we learned about two Assassin's Creed titles for the first time, it has also been reported that the development of Assassin's Creed Hexe is taking longer than expected. On Nov. 6, Ubisoft insider j0nathan posted a YouTube video in which he teased two new Assassin's Creed games. One is codenamed Mars and is reportedly a traditional Assassin's Creed game set in Ancient Rome, the same era in which the show's upcoming Netflix adaptation is set. The other is Assassin's Creed Pocket , a mobile game inspired by Valhalla's Mastery Challenges that will be set in Jerusalem. Insider Gaming followed up the next day to say that it'd heard of Assassin's Creed games with similar codenames, although it was not able to verify the projects enough to report on them first. It then revealed some more verified information about Assassin's Creed Hexe : While it was expected to be released in 2027, it has internally been pushed back to 2028. Assassin's Creed Hexe was first teased by Ubisoft in 2022 , and is supposed to have a more magical edge and be set in the Holy Roman Empire during the 17th century. While Ubisoft has promised to reveal more about the game next year, we've yet to actually see the game in action. According to Insider Gaming, Hexe's development has "had issues," with several high-level developers exiting Ubisoft during its development. Insider Gaming now does not expect Hexe to launch until 2028; in turn, it also reports that Mars likely wouldn't be released, or even revealed, until 2029 or 2030 at the earliest. For now, we'll just have to stick to playing Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced .
